And when the husband fears that the wife whom he demands may be suborned against him, the Judge ought to have her lodged and placed in a house where she fears neither force nor violence; as of old was done in a convent of nuns and religious women. <sup class="mk" data-key="l">l</sup>

notes.original: c. ex tranſmiſſa. c. literas. P. fin. de reſt. ſpel.
notes.gloss: A husband seeking restitution of a wife who fears his cruelty: she is meanwhile placed in a safe and honest house.

notes.citation: Decretals X 2.19.14 (De probationibus, the penultimate chapter, Causam matrimonii, Honorius III)
Decretals X 4.1 (De sponsalibus et matrimoniis), c. Cum locum (X 4.1.14)
notes.gloss: Where fear or coercion intervenes there is no room for consent; the woman is to be put in a place where she may freely declare her will — evidently for the sentence on lodging the wife "where she fears neither force nor violence".

english.html: Thus he makes in his hearing an ample and true discourse (as has since appeared) of the country of the Basques, of the father, mother, brothers, sisters and other kinsfolk of Martin Guerre; of the year, month and day of his wedding; of his father-in-law and mother-in-law; of the persons who were there, and who negotiated the marriage; of the robes and garments with which each was then attired; of the priest who married them; of all the particular acts that took place there, both on the day of the wedding and before and after, even to setting down the persons who, about midnight of the wedding, went to visit him in his bed. Moreover, of his pretended child Sanxi Guerre, and of the day he was born; of the cause of his departure; of the persons he met on the way, and of the talk they had had together; of the places where he had stayed during his absence, both in Spain and in France; and of the persons whom he had

uncertain.note: note key k has no {k} marker anywhere in the body; both readers checked every line at 3x-8x. The only markers printed are {i} (annotation line 3) and {l} (line 8). The note's key sits beside 'quer en vne maiſon, où elle ne redoute force, ni violen', so the omitted marker most likely belonged near 'ni violen-ce.' Compositor omission; note kept without a marker (standing ruling)

pages/strips/p038/margin-1.jpg, note l line 1. At 6x and 10x the sorts after 'penu' are: a tall italic l, then ONE short letter with a small hook at its top and no clear dot above (read as italic t, cf. the t of 'reſt' in note i; an italic i is the alternative), then round s, dotted i, hyphen: 'penultsi-' + 'me' on the next line. There is no second glyph between the l and the s, so A's 'penultisi-' has one letter too many. The expected citation is 'c. penultime de prob.'; the printed form is odd either way and is transcribed as printed

the line-end hyphen after 'tranſ' is only partly inked, a faint broken stroke at x-height, much lighter than the solid hyphens of 'lite-' and 'lo-'; read as a hyphen, could be an ink speck with the hyphen absent

pages/strips/p038/margin-1.jpg, note i line 4. (de restitutione spoliatorum); the letter is ink-filled and 'ſpol.' cannot be wholly excluded
